task: Register accountable persons with APRA and ASIC, keep accountability maps and statements up to date, notify changes, and defer senior executives' variable pay
basis: Analogue: taken from the impact statement for the Banking Executive Accountability Regime (BEAR), which the Financial Accountability Regime (FAR) replaced: Treasury estimated BEAR would cost $11.5 million a year for 149 authorised deposit-taking institutions (4 large, 20 medium, 125 small), upfront costs included, and the Office of Best Practice Regulation agreed the estimate. That is $77,181 an institution a year, taken here as 843 hours at today's work rate. It is in 2017 prices and not indexed. FAR also binds insurers and superannuation trustees, each assumed to cost the same as an average institution under BEAR. The low and high values (half and double) are assumed. No impact analysis costed FAR itself: its explanatory memorandum relies on the Royal Commission's final report, certified in place of one.
